question: Should the release/2026.7.1 durable-runtime stack expose persisted wake mutation through core CLI and Gateway APIs now, or should PR4 pause until the prerequisite runtime design is merged and the permanent operator contract is approved?
rationale: This adds a new core operator control plane over persisted session and delivery state; tests can validate mechanics, but automation cannot decide whether these commands and RPCs are the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve the stacked control surface
options.body: Sponsor the core CLI and Gateway API direction, require PR3 to land first, then finish documentation and live exact-head proof before merging this slice.

options.title: Keep inspection read-only
options.body: Allow list and inspect operations now but defer acknowledge, supersede, and mark mutations until their authorization, audit, and lifecycle contract is separately approved.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not promote later stack slices until maintainers accept or revise the underlying durable-runtime product direction.

recommendation.title: Approve the stacked control surface
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core CLI and Gateway API direction, require PR3 to land first, then finish documentation and live exact-head proof before merging this slice.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core runtime and release-line product-boundary decision rather than a narrow implementation repair.
